divergences.subject: invalid-frame
divergences.note: The server answers `initialize` with `"code": -32602.5`. We report BASE-007, the clause that names the defect; mcpsnoop's decoder refuses the frame and reports it as not JSON-RPC at all. Both are true — a non-integer code breaks JSON-RPC 2.0, which BASE-008 incorporates — and the two readings convict the same frame. The difference is only which clause carries the finding: ours attributes it to the most specific clause and leaves BASE-008 to framing faults, mcpsnoop has no rule finer than the parse.
divergences.resolution: none: the same defect on the same frame, reported at different granularity

divergences.subject: header-mismatch-unfounded
divergences.note: The trace is the fixture for the status rule alone: a `tools/list` whose every header matches its body is answered `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) with HTTP 500. Both tools report the status (TRAN-098, TRAN-102; mcpsnoop's `header-mismatch-status`). mcpsnoop also reports, in the same message, that the rejection had no cause: "every header on it agrees with the body". That is true of the trace, and we do not flag it: the revision says when a server must reject and names two cases in which it must not expect a header (TRAN-133, TRAN-135, a parameter that is `null` or absent, neither of which this request has), and no RFC 2119 sentence forbids a `-32020` on a matching request in general. mcpsnoop reads that as implied by the error code's meaning; the registry holds only what the text states.
divergences.resolution: none: no clause to hold the finding against; were the revision to state it, the check would follow

divergences.subject: BASE-030
divergences.note: Each trace's only request carries `"_meta": {}` — no protocol version anywhere, in the body or (base-032, HTTP) in a header. We judge the trace at `2026-07-28` because the corpus files it under `draft/`, which is how this repository assigns a revision; mcpsnoop infers the revision from the session and finds none, so it applies no `2026-07-28` rule. Given what each tool is told, each is right: an empty `_meta` is a violation at `2026-07-28` and none at `2025-11-25`. mcpsnoop does flag the same field set as missing wherever the session names `2026-07-28` (base-030-request-meta-missing-required-field and the probe capture agree with us).
divergences.resolution: none: the revision is stated to our validator out of band and is absent from the trace

divergences.subject: TOOL-016

divergences.subject: BASE-030
divergences.note: A legacy client sends `initialize` naming `2025-11-25`. In vers-008 the server speaks only `2026-07-28` and refuses; in base-030-legacy-initialize-negotiated-2026-07-28 it answers naming `2026-07-28` and the session goes on under it. Judging the whole trace at `2026-07-28` (the corpus's `draft/` assignment for the first; the server's `initialize` result, which is the session's revision, for the second), we report the `initialize` as a request missing the required `_meta` fields — deliberately: `checks/stateless/meta.rs` exempts this request from BASE-031, citing `basic/versioning`'s compatibility matrix (which says of exactly this request that it "also lacks the required `_meta` fields"), and states that the client's own defect is still reported, by BASE-030. mcpsnoop draws nothing on either trace, at 0.28.0 as at 0.26.1. Measured 2026-10-25 with 0.26.1, and not repeated since, on edited copies of the second trace's converted capture: it applies `request-meta-missing` to a request only when that request's own `_meta` carries `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` `2026-07-28` (an `initialize` whose `_meta` names it and lacks the other fields is flagged, so `initialize` is not exempt); a request with no `_meta`, an empty one, or one naming `2025-11-25` draws nothing, and setting the `initialize` params' `protocolVersion` to `2026-07-28` changes nothing. So its per-request revision is the one the request states in `_meta`, not `params.protocolVersion` and not the server's answer; an earlier version of this note said it reads the request's own `protocolVersion`, which that measurement does not support. Whether a `2026-07-28` clause binds a request that is itself speaking `2025-11-25` is not settled by the text: the matrix describes the request as lacking the fields without saying the legacy client is non-conformant for it, and nothing makes a `2025-11-25` client subject to `2026-07-28`. The same question sits under our TRAN-071 finding on the probe capture's legacy `initialize`.
divergences.resolution: open: decide whether a legacy-era request inside a 2026-07-28 trace is held to that revision's request-envelope clauses (BASE-030 and its restatements, TRAN-071); the current reading is recorded in `checks/stateless/meta.rs`

divergences.subject: progress-after-completion
divergences.note: A conforming `2025-11-25` task session: the server answers a task-augmented `tools/call` with a `CreateTaskResult` (seq 4) and sends progress under the request's token while the task is `working` (seq 5, and seq 10 after a `tasks/get` that still says `working`); the task is `completed` only at seq 12. The tasks page has the token "continue to be used for progress notifications throughout the task's lifetime, even after the `CreateTaskResult` has been returned" (PROG-014) and stops progress at the task's terminal status (PROG-016), which this session respects; our validator passes it. mcpsnoop warns on both notifications as arriving "after its request completed", with the text "2026-07-28 requires them to stop": it takes the `CreateTaskResult` for the request's completion and applies that revision's rule to a `2025-11-25` session. The same rule fires, correctly, on prog-019 (progress after an ordinary response) and, for the earlier of its two notifications, wrongly on prog-016 for the same reason as here; both traces agree with us at the trace level.
divergences.resolution: open: whether to report it upstream is the maintainer's call; the reproduction is `corpus/good/stdio-task-progress.jsonl`, whose task handling the `2025-11-25` tasks page defines (PROG-014)
